$comment: D-ASM-SUB-NATIVE-OPERAND-UNUSABLE-IN-INLINE-ASM: the first runnable witness that a `char` or a `short` can be a GNU extended-asm operand. ★★★ THIS EXAMPLE WAS BORN RED. ✔MEASURED through the real CLI on a clean HEAD build, x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec and x86_64:elf64-x86_64-linux-exec at debug AND release: `__asm__("movb %1, %0" : "=r"(r) : "r"(v))` on `char` operands was `error[A0008] unknown mnemonic 'movb' — it is not in this dialect's instruction table`, `movw` the same at width 16, and the `movl`-on-a-char alternative was `error[A0008] 'movl' declares operand width 32, but its register operands are 8 bits`. Every inline-asm example already in the tree binds an `int`/`long`/`long long`, and that was not taste — it was the only thing that worked. ✔THE REFERENCE DISJUNCTION, MEASURED: gcc 13.3.0 compiles AND RUNS all twelve shapes at -O0 and -O2 (exit 42), and REFUSES the `movl`-on-a-char spelling exactly as DSS does, so conformance runs both ways. ★★★ THE DEFECT THIS EXAMPLE EXISTS TO CATCH IS SILENT, WHICH IS WHY SHAPES 8 AND 9 LOOK ODD: AT&T `movb (%rax), %cl` is `8A /r` and writes ONLY `cl`, while the target's width-8 `load` row is `0F B6` (MOVZX, which gas spells `movzbl`) and ZEROES the upper bits. Both assemble, both run, and nothing reads the difference unless a bit ABOVE the written field is required to survive — which is what those two shapes do: a zero-extending encoding returns 42 where the correct one returns 298 / 65578. This is why the memory-source direction is a SEPARATE opcode (`load_subreg`) rather than a variant on `load`: one (opcode, operandKinds, width) triple cannot denote two machine instructions, and the schema loader refuses the attempt. ★★ TWELVE SHAPES, EACH ITS OWN EXIT CODE: (1,2) register-to-register byte and word moves; (3) an immediate into a byte register (`C6 /0 ib`, riding the existing 1-byte slot); (4,5) memory SOURCE at 8 and 16 bits, i.e. `load_subreg`; (6,7) memory DESTINATION on a global, so the address is a relocated symbol; (8,9) the zero-extension DISCRIMINATORS; (10,11) an operand whose source register provably holds bits ABOVE its own width; (12) HAND-WRITTEN narrow register spellings (`%ax`, `%dl`), which is what the 16-bit `registers[]` rows exist for — a bound `%N` never needs them because its width comes from `AsmOperandBinding::widthBits`, but `%ax` written in the text does. ★★★ SHAPES 10 AND 11 ARE THE MEASUREMENT OF A LABELLED SUSPECT: `MirToLir::emitAsmOperandMove` emits an operand's materialisation copy at the target's default width (64) regardless of the operand's `widthBits`, and the trigger could not fire while `char`/`short` were refused. ✔MEASURED in the emitted code once it could — `mov %r15,%r15` (REX.W 8B /r) ahead of `mov %r15b,%r15b` — and it is VALUE-CORRECT on this target: a full-register copy preserves the low N bits exactly, and the output capture re-reads at the operand's own width (`movsbq`/`movswq`), so the upper bits never reach a consumer un-recast. These two shapes hold that conclusion by execution rather than by argument. ⛔ NO aarch64 TARGET, AND THE CLAUSE THAT USED TO EXPLAIN WHY WAS FALSE — CORRECTED IN PLACE FOR THE SECOND TIME, WHICH IS THE REUSABLE PART. It SAID a `char` operand was still refused on that CPU, and that whether to substitute the 64-bit `x` view instead — as gcc and clang do — was an open OPERATOR decision whose two arms answered this exact question oppositely. That decision was taken and has SHIPPED: `D-ASM-BARE-OPERAND-WIDTH-DIVERGES-FROM-REFERENCE` IS CLOSED (P42 lane AG), arm64 declares `asmBareOperandWidths` `gpr` = `registerNatural`, and the refusal is NO LONGER there. ✔RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 through the CLI on arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-exec, in BOTH directions, against a config root carrying the pre-fix derivation so the counterfactual is a measurement rather than a memory: the ALU shape `add %0, %1, %2` over two `char` operands WAS refused under the old rule (`error[A_AsmTextUnsupported]: register '%0' is 64 bits wide but register '%1' is 8 bits`) and now COMPILES and runs to 42 under qemu-aarch64 — gcc 13.3.0 runs the identical source to 42 as well; and the `=m` store shape emitted `strb`/`strh` under the old rule (a 1- and a 2-byte store, exit 1) against `str x15, [x16]` and exit 42 now. ⇒ what survives is only the NARROW fact that THIS example declares no aarch64 arm, and the reason is its own `main.c` rather than any refusal: it is guarded `#if !defined(__x86_64__)` with an `#error`, so giving it one means writing that arm in the PROGRAM, not declaring a target in this manifest. The aarch64 coverage for a sub-native operand lives in `examples/c/c_inline_asm_bare_operand_width`, whose aarch64 arm binds a `char` and executes it. ★★★ THE SHAPE, NOW WITNESSED TWICE IN THIS ONE FILE: a sentence that pins a REFUSAL to an OPEN row has a shelf life exactly as long as that row's. The first version said `movw $imm, %reg` STAYS REFUSED, citing a row a sibling lane closed in the same commit; this one said a `char` operand STAYS REFUSED, citing the very row whose closure is what made it work. Both were written carefully, by lanes that had measured the thing they described, and both rotted within the week. The durable form states the MECHANISM and the measurement DATE and lets the row's own status cell carry the status. ⚠⚠ THIS SENTENCE SHIPPED FALSE AND IS CORRECTED IN PLACE RATHER THAN DELETED, BECAUSE THE SHAPE IS THE REUSABLE PART. It said `movw $imm, %reg` STAYS REFUSED, citing a row a sibling lane closed IN THE SAME COMMIT. The mechanism it named was real: a 16-bit immediate is `66 C7 /0 iw` and the x86-variable encoder used to declare no 2-byte immediate slot, so emitting the 4-byte one would have corrupted the instruction stream silently — which is why it was fail-loud rather than approximated. The slot now exists (`EncodingSlotKind::Imm16Bytes`) and D-ASM-X86-NO-16BIT-IMMEDIATE-SLOT is CLOSED; ✔RE-MEASURED at the CLI, `movw $42` into an `=r` short compiles rc=0 and RUNS at debug and release. Shape 3 still spells the BYTE form because the 1-byte slot is what it exists to test. ⇒ a cross-lane citation of an OPEN row is a claim with an expiry date, and the fold is when it expires (D-COMMENT-A-CLAIM-TRUE-WHEN-TYPED-AND-FALSE-WHEN-THE-COMMIT-LANDED). ⚠ The `volatile` seeds are load-bearing: without them the release pipeline folds the values before lowering and silently changes which mechanism each arm tests.
